# Getting Started using the REST API

The REST API is the main way of obtaining the Pokemon TCG information you search.

## Usage

[Section titled “Usage”](https://tcgdex.dev/rest#usage)

You can use the REST API multiple ways.

1. Using one of the [SDKs](https://tcgdex.dev/sdks)
2. Querying directly one the API

Everything is detailled in the documentation to allow you to do both.

[Try one of our SDKs](https://tcgdex.dev/sdks)

[Look at the API](https://tcgdex.dev/rest/card)

## Information

[Section titled “Information”](https://tcgdex.dev/rest#information)

- The REST API returns predictable Objects defined under each request.
- It is only available in HTTPS (HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS)
- Every request MUST be GET requests.
- the API returns JSON responses in the body
- We use standard HTTP response codes and every response possibles are indicated on each pages

## History

[Section titled “History”](https://tcgdex.dev/rest#history)

### V2

[Section titled “V2”](https://tcgdex.dev/rest#v2)

The V2 of the API is the current one and was first enabled on January 2021.

It currently Achieve more than 10 Millions requests per months.

### V1

[Section titled “V1”](https://tcgdex.dev/rest#v1)

The V1 of the API was active from february 2020 to August 2021.

It achived at it’s peak (february 2021) Around 200k requests per month.

The V1 was deprecated in february 2021 and was completelly removed after 6 month in deprecation with :

- All SDKs working with the v2
- receiving less than 1k requests per month during the two previous months on it.

# Getting a single card

## Request

[Section titled “Request”](https://tcgdex.dev/rest/card#request)

- [PHP](https://tcgdex.dev/rest/card#tab-panel-12)
- [Javascript](https://tcgdex.dev/rest/card#tab-panel-13)
- [Typescript](https://tcgdex.dev/rest/card#tab-panel-14)
- [Java](https://tcgdex.dev/rest/card#tab-panel-15)
- [Kotlin](https://tcgdex.dev/rest/card#tab-panel-16)
- [cURL](https://tcgdex.dev/rest/card#tab-panel-17)

```
$card = $tcgdex->card->get('swsh3-136');
```

_[See how to setup the PHP SDK](https://tcgdex.dev/sdks/php)_

```
const card = await tcgdex.card.get('swsh3-136');
```

_[See how to setup the Javascript SDK](https://tcgdex.dev/sdks/javascript)_

```
const card = await tcgdex.card.getCard('swsh3-136');
```

_[See how to setup the Typescript SDK](https://tcgdex.dev/sdks/typescript)_

```
Card card = tcgdex.fetchCard("swsh3-136");

_[See how to setup the Java SDK](https://tcgdex.dev/sdks/java)_

```
val card = tcgdex.fetchCard("swsh3-136")
```

_[See how to setup the Kotlin SDK](https://tcgdex.dev/sdks/kotlin)_

```
https://api.tcgdex.net/v2/en/cards/swsh3-136

_[See how to prepare your URLs](https://tcgdex.dev/rest)_

# Frequently Asked Questions

## Variants & Card Data

[Section titled “Variants & Card Data”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#variants--card-data)

### How do normal / reverse / holo variants work?

[Section titled “How do normal / reverse / holo variants work?”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#how-do-normal--reverse--holo-variants-work)

Each card object currently contains a `variants` field that describes which printings are known to exist:

```
"variants": {

  "normal": true,

  "reverse": true,

  "holo": false,

  "firstEdition": false

}
```

A value of `true` means that printing is known to exist. The upcoming `variants_detailed` field will expand on this by including marketplace-specific IDs for each variant, enabling more accurate pricing and data lookups.

If a variant is showing clearly incorrect data for a specific set (for example, Ascended Heroes variants), you’re welcome to report it via [Discord](https://tcgdex.dev/discord) or a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/tcgdex/cards-database/issues), though many known issues are already captured as part of the ongoing improvements.

### Why is a card missing from a set, or showing the wrong local ID?

[Section titled “Why is a card missing from a set, or showing the wrong local ID?”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#why-is-a-card-missing-from-a-set-or-showing-the-wrong-local-id)

Card data is community-maintained. If you notice a missing card or an incorrect `localId`, you can contribute a fix directly in the [cards database repository](https://github.com/tcgdex/cards-database).

* * *

## Images

[Section titled “Images”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#images)

### Why are some card images missing?

[Section titled “Why are some card images missing?”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#why-are-some-card-images-missing)

Card images are hosted separately from the card data. An image URL will be present in the API response when the image has been contributed and processed. If a card has no `image` field, the image has not yet been added to the database.

### How do I contribute a missing card image?

[Section titled “How do I contribute a missing card image?”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#how-do-i-contribute-a-missing-card-image)

At the moment, image contributions are handled through the [Discord community](https://tcgdex.dev/discord). Reach out there and a maintainer will guide you through the process.

### Why does an image URL have no file extension?

[Section titled “Why does an image URL have no file extension?”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#why-does-an-image-url-have-no-file-extension)

This is intentional — see the [Assets Management](https://tcgdex.dev/assets) page for a full explanation. You append the quality and extension yourself:

```
https://assets.tcgdex.net/en/swsh/swsh3/136/high.webp

https://assets.tcgdex.net/en/swsh/swsh3/136/low.png
```

* * *

## Contributing & Reporting Issues

[Section titled “Contributing & Reporting Issues”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#contributing--reporting-issues)

### How do I report incorrect data?

[Section titled “How do I report incorrect data?”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#how-do-i-report-incorrect-data)

- **Discord** — fastest way to get a response: [tcgdex.dev/discord](https://tcgdex.dev/discord)
- **GitHub Issues** — for bugs and data errors: [cards-database issues](https://github.com/tcgdex/cards-database/issues/new?assignees=&labels=issue%2Cserver&projects=&template=api-issue.yml&title=issue%3A)

Please include the affected card ID (e.g. `bw10-99`) and a description of what is wrong and what the correct value should be.

### How do I contribute card data or translations?

[Section titled “How do I contribute card data or translations?”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#how-do-i-contribute-card-data-or-translations)

The card database is open source. You can submit pull requests to add missing cards, fix data, or add translations:

[cards-database on GitHub](https://github.com/tcgdex/cards-database) The main repository for all card data and translations

[Join our Discord](https://tcgdex.dev/discord) Ask questions and get help before contributing

Translation files live in the `meta/translations` directory of the repository.

* * *

## General API Questions

[Section titled “General API Questions”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#general-api-questions)

### Is authentication required?

[Section titled “Is authentication required?”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#is-authentication-required)

No. The TCGdex API is free to use and requires no API key.

### Are there rate limits?

[Section titled “Are there rate limits?”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#are-there-rate-limits)

There are no published hard rate limits, but please be considerate. For bulk data needs, cache responses locally rather than fetching the same data repeatedly.

### What formats does the API support?

[Section titled “What formats does the API support?”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#what-formats-does-the-api-support)

The REST API returns JSON. A [GraphQL API](https://tcgdex.dev/graphql) is also available for more flexible querying.

### Which languages are supported?

[Section titled “Which languages are supported?”](https://tcgdex.dev/faq#which-languages-are-supported)

The API supports over 10 languages including English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazilian), Japanese, Chinese (Traditional), Indonesian, and Thai. See the [project status page](https://tcgdex.dev/status) for current completion levels per language.

**The Pokémon TCG API is deprecated.**
New account registrations are no longer available.
Existing API keys will continue to function through March 1, 2027.

## Attributes [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#attributes "Direct link to heading")

### **id** _string_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#id-string "Direct link to heading")

Unique identifier for the object.

* * *

### **name** _string_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#name-string "Direct link to heading")

The name of the card.

* * *

### **supertype** _string_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#supertype-string "Direct link to heading")

The supertype of the card, such as Pokémon, Energy, or Trainer.

* * *

### **subtypes** _list(string)_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#subtypes-liststring "Direct link to heading")

A list of subtypes, such as Basic, EX, Mega, Rapid Strike, etc.

* * *

### **level** _string_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#level-string "Direct link to heading")

The level of the card. This only pertains to cards from older sets and those of supertype Pokémon.

* * *

### **hp** _string_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#hp-string "Direct link to heading")

The hit points of the card.

* * *

### **types** _list(string)_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#types-liststring "Direct link to heading")

The energy types for a card, such as Fire, Water, Grass, etc.

* * *

### **evolvesFrom** _string_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#evolvesfrom-string "Direct link to heading")

Which Pokémon this card evolves from.

* * *

### **evolvesTo** _list(string)_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#evolvesto-liststring "Direct link to heading")

Which Pokémon this card evolves to. Can be multiple, for example, Eevee.

* * *

### **rules** _list(string)_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#rules-liststring "Direct link to heading")

Any rules associated with the card. For example, VMAX rules, Mega rules, or various trainer rules.

* * *

### **ancientTrait** _hash_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#ancienttrait-hash "Direct link to heading")

The ancient trait for a given card. An ancient trait has the following fields:

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **name** _string_ | The name of the ancient trait |
| **text** _string_ | The text value of the ancient trait |

* * *

### **abilities** _list(hash)_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#abilities-listhash "Direct link to heading")

One or more abilities for a given card. An ability has the following fields:

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **name** _string_ | The name of the ability |
| **text** _string_ | The text value of the ability |
| **type** _string_ | The type of the ability, such as Ability or Pokémon-Power |

* * *

### **attacks** _list(hash)_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#attacks-listhash "Direct link to heading")

One or more attacks for a given card. An attack has the following fields:

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **cost** _list(string)_ | The cost of the attack represented by a list of energy types. |
| **name** _string_ | The name of the attack |
| **text** _string_ | The text or description associated with the attack |
| **damage** _string_ | The damage amount of the attack |
| **convertedEnergyCost** _integer_ | The total cost of the attack. For example, if it costs 2 fire energy, the converted energy cost is simply 2. |

### **weaknesses** _list(hash)_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#weaknesses-listhash "Direct link to heading")

One or more weaknesses for a given card. A weakness has the following fields:

| **type** _string_ | The type of weakness, such as Fire or Water. |

### **retreatCost** _list(string)_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#retreatcost-liststring "Direct link to heading")

A list of costs it takes to retreat and return the card to your bench. Each cost is an energy type, such as Water or Fire.

### **convertedRetreatCost** _integer_ [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/api-reference/cards/card-object/\#convertedretreatcost-integer "Direct link to heading")

The converted retreat cost for a card is the count of energy types found within the retreatCost field. For example, \["Fire", "Water"\] has a
converted retreat cost of 2.

The set details embedded into the card. See the set object for more details.

## Overview [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/getting-started/rate-limits/\#overview "Direct link to heading")

Rate limits are enforced for all third-party applications and services. This document is an overview of the rate limits themselves, as well as how they are enforced and best practices for handling the errors returned when a rate limit is reached.

## V2 Rate Limits [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/getting-started/rate-limits/\#v2-rate-limits "Direct link to heading")

Third-party application rate limits depend on your API key. By default, requests are limited to 20,000/day. If you need a higher rate limit, feel free to contact me via Discord or email and we can discuss.

If you aren’t using an API key, you are rate limited to 1000 requests a day, and a maxium of 30 per minute.

## V1 (Deprecated) Rate Limits [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/getting-started/rate-limits/\#v1-deprecated-rate-limits "Direct link to heading")

Third-party applications are currently throttled to 30 requests per minute. As this API continues to age, the rate limits may be updated to provide better performance to users

## Rationale [\#](https://docs.pokemontcg.io/getting-started/rate-limits/\#rationale "Direct link to heading")

As previously mentioned, the primary goal is to provide a responsive interface for developers and users to use when accessing the Pokémon TCG data. Since each request made to the API incurs a computational cost, it’s in the best interest of both the Pokémon TCG API and its developer partners that these costs be minimized to the greatest degree possible.

Rate limiting also helps third-party developers by encouraging them to build their integrations to make economical use of API requests.

By donating to this API via Patreon or Kofi, you can help ensure that the server performance will meet your application needs.
